# Sampletable

```{r data}
subgroup_i <- params$subgroup
spt <- read.csv('../config/sampletable.tsv', sep='\t')
knitr::kable(spt %>%
             select(-layout, -Run)
                )
samples <- spt %>%
    filter(fraction == 'IP', subgroup == subgroup_i) %>%
    .[['samplename']]

if (length(samples) == 0) {
    cat(paste0('\n\nNo IP samples correspond to the subgroup ', subgroup_i, ', this analysis is not run.\n\n'))
    knitr::knit_exit()
}
```





```{r read_xlsx, cache=TRUE}
fns <- list(
    'reads' = paste0('Summary_interactions_with_IP_', subgroup_i, '.xlsx'),
    'chimeras' = paste0('Summary_RILSeq_S-chimeras_', subgroup_i, '.xlsx')
    )

sheet_names <- list(
    'reads' = c('RILseq_all_chimeras', 'RILseq_singles', 'Total_RNAseq'),
    'chimeras' = samples
    )

res_list <- list()

for (nm in names(fns)) {
  res_list[[nm]] <- lapply(sheet_names[[nm]], function(x){
    read.xlsx(fns[[nm]], sheet=x)
  })
  names(res_list[[nm]]) <- sheet_names[[nm]]
}
```

# Mapped reads distribution

Here we used the TPM counts from `r fns[['reads']]`, summed per feature type. The results are plotted
in stacked bar graphs.


```{r prep_histogram, results='asis', cache=TRUE, dependson='read_xlsx'}
common_cols <- c('Geneid', 'Chr', 'Start', 'End', 'Strand', 'Length', 'Type', paste0('FPM_', samples))

conv_type <- list(
  "empty"='other',
  "3UTR"="3UTR",
  "5UTR"="5UTR",
  "AS"="AS",
  "IGR"="IGR",
  "IGT"="IGT",
  "cis_AS_with_trans_t"="other",
  "mRNA"="mRNA",
  "other-ncRNA"="other",
  "rRNA"="rRNA",
  "sRNA"="sRNA",
  "tRNA"="tRNA"
)


dir.create('plots', showWarnings = FALSE)

plot_dist_hist <- function(df.i, label) {
    df.i <- df.i %>%
        tidyr::pivot_longer(starts_with('FPM'), values_to='TPM', names_to='samples') %>%
        # simplify sample names
        mutate(samples = gsub('FPM_', '', samples)) %>%
        # simplify categories
        mutate(Type = ifelse(Type == "", 'empty', Type))
    df.i[['Type']] <- conv_type[df.i[['Type']]] %>% unlist()

    # aggregate by Type
    df.i <- df.i %>%
        group_by(Type, samples) %>%
        summarize(Cumulative_sum_TPM=sum(TPM))

    # samples as factor to plot in same order
    df.i[['samples']] <- factor(df.i[['samples']], levels=unique(df.i[['samples']]))

    p <- ggplot(df.i, aes(x=samples, y=Cumulative_sum_TPM, fill=Type)) +
      geom_bar(stat='identity') +
      theme_classic() +
      theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust=1))

    print(p)
    fn <- paste0('plots/barplot_', label, '.pdf')
    ggsave(fn)
    cat(paste0('\n\n- [', fn, '](', fn, ')\n\n'))
}

for (nm in names(res_list[['reads']])) {
  cat(paste0('\n\n## ', nm, '\n\n'))
  if (all(common_cols %in% names(res_list[['reads']][[nm]]))) {
    plot_dist_hist(res_list[['reads']][[nm]][common_cols], nm)
  } else {
    cat('\n\nFPM for those samples were not processed.\n\n')
  }
}
```


# S-Chimera distribution


```{r pie_prep, results='asis', cache=TRUE, dependson='read_xlsx'}
# aggregate all samples into 1 df
# don't need untagged
samples <- samples[!grepl('Untagged', samples)]
res_sub <- res_list[['chimeras']][samples]

# make the categories for RNA1 and RNA2 types, follow the hierarchy:
# - contains both sRNA and mRNA
# - sRNA ORF (but not mRNA)
# - mRNA (but not sRNA)
# - both 5UTR and 3UTR
# - 5UTR (but not 3UTR)
# - 3UTR (but not 5 UTR)
# - AS
# - IGR
# - other

get_hierarchical_category <- function(x) {
    if (grepl('mRNA', x) & grepl('sRNA', x)) {
        return('mRNA_and_sRNA')
    } else if (grepl('mRNA', x)) {
        return('mRNA')
    } else if (grepl('sRNA', x)) {
        return('sRNA')
    } else if (grepl('5UTR', x) & grepl('3UTR', x)) {
        return('5UTR_and_3UTR')
    } else if (grepl('5UTR', x)) {
        return('5UTR')
    } else if (grepl('3UTR', x)) {
        return('3UTR')
    } else if (grepl('AS', x)) {
        return('AS')
    } else if (grepl('IGR', x)) {
        return('IGR')
    } else {
        return('other')
    }
}

# assign the RNA categories and make pairs (1 sorted and 1 non sorted to distinguish sRNA-mRNA from mRNA-sRNA)
res_sub <- lapply(res_sub, function(x) {
    x[['TypeRNA1']] <- lapply(x[['TypeRNA1']], get_hierarchical_category) %>% unlist()
    x[['TypeRNA2']] <- lapply(x[['TypeRNA2']], get_hierarchical_category) %>% unlist()
    x[['sorted_pair']] <- lapply(rownames(x), function(y) {
        paste0(sort(c(x[y,'TypeRNA1'], x[y, 'TypeRNA2']), decreasing=TRUE), collapse='-')
    }) %>% unlist()
    x[['ordered_pair']] <- lapply(rownames(x), function(y) {
        paste0(c(x[y,'TypeRNA1'], x[y, 'TypeRNA2']), collapse='-')
    }) %>% unlist()
#    x[['chimera_fraction']] <- 1/dim(x)[[1]]
#    x[['interactions_fraction']] <- x[['interactions']] / sum(x[['interactions']])
    return(x)
})

# aggregate samples into 1 df
res_sub <- do.call(rbind, res_sub)

# first group by ID to get the totals
totals <- res_sub %>%
    select(sorted_pair, ID, interactions) %>%
    group_by(ID) %>%
    summarize(total_chimera = n(), total_interactions = sum(interactions))

# merge the totals and group by sorted pair
df.i <- merge(res_sub, totals) %>%
    group_by(sorted_pair, ID) %>%
    reframe(
        'chimera_fraction' = n()/total_chimera,
        'interactions_fraction' = sum(interactions)/total_interactions
    ) %>%
    distinct()

# too many small categories, group them
# take the max among samples of each category and take the top X categories
to_keep <- df.i %>%
    group_by(sorted_pair) %>%
    summarize(
        max_chimera = max(chimera_fraction),
        max_interactions = max(interactions_fraction)) %>%
    arrange(desc(max_interactions)) %>%
    slice(1:10) %>%
    .[['sorted_pair']]
# some categories are related and should be grouped
to_group <- c('mRNA_and_sRNA-mRNA', 'sRNA-mRNA_and_sRNA', 'mRNA_and_sRNA-mRNA_and_sRNA')

# add simplified pair column and recalculate the group_by 
res_sub <- res_sub %>%
    mutate(simplified_pair = ifelse(
        sorted_pair %in% c(to_keep, to_group), sorted_pair, 'other')) %>%
    mutate(simplified_pair = ifelse(
        simplified_pair %in% to_group, 'overlapping_sRNAs_and_mRNAs', simplified_pair))

totals <- res_sub %>%
    select(simplified_pair, ID, interactions) %>%
    group_by(ID) %>%
    summarize(total_chimera = n(), total_interactions = sum(interactions))

# merge the totals and group by sorted pair
df.i <- merge(res_sub, totals) %>%
    group_by(simplified_pair, ID) %>%
    reframe(
        'chimera_fraction' = n()/total_chimera,
        'interactions_fraction' = sum(interactions)/total_interactions
    ) %>%
    distinct()

# rearrange the sample order, to have WT first
df.i[['ID']] <- factor(df.i[['ID']], levels=unique(df.i[['ID']]))
```

In this section, we used Summary_RILSeq_S-chimeras.xlsx as input to plot the distribution of chimera
feature pairs (RNA1-RNA2).

The categories are assigned with hierarchical rules for RNA1, then RNA2:

- contains both sRNA and mRNA (called mRNA_and_sRNA)
- sRNA (but not mRNA)
- mRNA (but not sRNA)
- both 5UTR and 3UTR
- 5UTR (but not 3UTR)
- 3UTR (but not 5 UTR)
- AS
- IGR
- other

The chimera pairs are assigned a name made of alphabetically sorted RNA1 and RNA2, separated by a dash.
The order of RNA1 and RNA2 is not taken into account (i.e.
mRNA-sRNA and sRNA-mRNA are both categorized in ``sRNA-mRNA``).

We decided to subset the pair categories to the most informative.

The 10 most abundant categories in term of number of
supporting interactions returned:

```{r, results='asis'}
for (c in to_keep) {
    cat(paste0('\n\n- ', c, '\n\n'))
}

cat('\n\nThe following categories are related and will be grouped under ``overlapping_sRNAs_and_mRNAs``:\n\n')

for (c in to_group) {
    cat(paste0('\n\n- ', c, '\n\n'))
}
```

All other, less abundant, categories will be grouped under ``other``.

```{r plot_pie, results='asis', cache=TRUE, dependson='pie_prep', fig.height=10}
cat('\n\n## Fraction of chimera\n\n')
ggplot(df.i, aes(x='', y = chimera_fraction, fill = simplified_pair)) +
  geom_col(color='black', linewidth=0.2) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y", start = 0) + 
  facet_wrap(vars(ID), ncol = 2) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 10)) +
  ggtitle('Distribution of chimera')

fn <- 'plots/pie_chart_chimera_fraction.pdf'
ggsave(fn, width = 15, height = 15, units = "cm", dpi=600)
cat(paste0('\n\n- [', fn, '](', fn, ')\n\n'))

cat('\n\n## Fraction of total interaction numbers\n\n')
ggplot(df.i, aes(x='', y = interactions_fraction, fill = simplified_pair)) +
  geom_col(color='black', linewidth=0.2) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y", start = 0) + 
  facet_wrap(vars(ID), ncol = 2) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 10)) + 
  ggtitle('Distribution of interactions')

fn <- 'plots/pie_chart_interactions_fraction.pdf'
ggsave(fn, width = 15, height = 15, units = "cm", dpi=600)
cat(paste0('\n\n- [', fn, '](', fn, ')\n\n'))

```

# sRNA order in RNA1 or RNA2

Below are pie charts for sRNA-mRNA and sRNA-5’UTR respectively, showing the distribution
of whether sRNAs were assigned to RNA1 or RNA2. This is to confirm whether most sRNAs still
occupy RNA2 position.


```{r position, results='asis'}
# want to group by ordered pairs, but recalculate the fractions relative to the simplified pairs
totals <- res_sub %>%
    select(simplified_pair, ID, interactions) %>%
    group_by(ID, simplified_pair) %>%
    summarize(total_chimera = n(), total_interactions = sum(interactions))

# merge the totals and group by sorted pair
# note that the ordered_pair has not been simplified. Categories modified in simplification will be wrong here
df.i <- merge(res_sub, totals) %>%
    group_by(ordered_pair, ID) %>%
    reframe(
        'chimera_fraction' = n()/total_chimera,
        'interactions_fraction' = sum(interactions)/total_interactions,
        'ordered_pair' = unique(ordered_pair),
        'simplified_pair' = unique(simplified_pair)
    ) %>%
    distinct()

# rearrange the sample order, to have WT first
df.i[['ID']] <- factor(df.i[['ID']], levels=unique(df.i[['ID']]))

# color-coordinating with full list pie charts
cols <- list(
    'sRNA-mRNA' = c('#873DBF', '#C48DEB'),
    'sRNA-5UTR' = c('#42A15A', '#85D99B')
    )

for (categ in c('sRNA-mRNA', 'sRNA-5UTR')) {
    # filter to sRNA-mRNA interactions only, 
    cat('\n\n## Fraction of chimera\n\n')
    p <- ggplot(df.i %>% filter(simplified_pair == categ),
        aes(x='', y = chimera_fraction, fill = ordered_pair)) +
      geom_col(color='black', linewidth=0.2) +
      coord_polar(theta = "y", start = 0) + 
      facet_wrap(vars(ID), ncol = 2) +
      theme_void() +
      scale_fill_manual(values=cols[[categ]]) +
      theme(text = element_text(size = 10)) +
      ggtitle('Distribution of chimera')
    print(p)

    fn <- paste0('plots/pie_chart_chimera_', categ, '_order.pdf')
    ggsave(fn, width = 15, height = 15, units = "cm", dpi=600)
    cat(paste0('\n\n- [', fn, '](', fn, ')\n\n'))

    cat('\n\n## Fraction of total interaction numbers\n\n')
    p <- ggplot(df.i %>% filter(simplified_pair == categ),
        aes(x='', y = interactions_fraction, fill = ordered_pair)) +
      geom_col(color='black', linewidth=0.2) +
      coord_polar(theta = "y", start = 0) + 
      facet_wrap(vars(ID), ncol = 2) +
      theme_void() +
      scale_fill_manual(values=cols[[categ]]) +
      theme(text = element_text(size = 10)) + 
      ggtitle('Distribution of interactions')
    print(p)

    fn <- paste0('plots/pie_chart_interactions_', categ, 'order.pdf')
    ggsave(fn, width = 15, height = 15, units = "cm", dpi=600)
    cat(paste0('\n\n- [', fn, '](', fn, ')\n\n'))
}
```
